LESSON: MY FAMILY FAMILY MEMBERS

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
Strand: Creation
Topic 1.4: My Family Family members

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on My Family Family members. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why is it important to know members of your family?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. name family members in the nuclear and extended family
2. draw a family tree to understand relationships within the family
3. explain why it is important to honour parents
4. respect family members for harmonious co- existence
5. identify whom to report to if touched inappropriately or sexually abused
6. appreciate the body as a temple of the Holy Spirit and live a holy life

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: MY FAMILY FAMILY MEMBERS
Subject: CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION · Grade: Grade 4
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
My Family Family members helps you succeed in CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION. You will understand it, practise it, and use it in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

KEY FACTS: MY FAMILY FAMILY MEMBERS
Good citizens follow rules, respect others, and care for shared places.
Kenyan examples: lining up, keeping the compound clean, telling the truth, helping a classmate.
Rights come with responsibilities.

PART 1: Name family members in the nuclear and extended family

What this means
In this part you learn to name family members in the nuclear and extended family. You will use ideas from in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: name family members in the nuclear and extended family.
2. Locate, explain, then act responsibly using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Locate: Connect “My Family Family members” to a real place or group in Kenya (school, market, county office, home).

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can name family members in the nuclear and extended family. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Draw a family tree to understand relationships within the family

What this means
In this part you learn to draw a family tree to understand relationships within the family. You will use ideas from in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: draw a family tree to understand relationships within the family.
2. Locate, explain, then act responsibly using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Explain: Give one cause and one effect linked to My Family Family members.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can draw a family tree to understand relationships within the family. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Explain why it is important to honour parents

What this means
In this part you learn to explain why it is important to honour parents. You will use ideas from in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: explain why it is important to honour parents.
2. Locate, explain, then act responsibly using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Participate: Describe one responsible action a Grade learner can take.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can explain why it is important to honour parents. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 4: Respect family members for harmonious co- existence

What this means
In this part you learn to respect family members for harmonious co- existence. You will use ideas from in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: respect family members for harmonious co- existence.
2. Locate, explain, then act responsibly using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Locate: Connect “My Family Family members” to a real place or group in Kenya (school, market, county office, home).

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can respect family members for harmonious co- existence. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 5: Identify whom to report to if touched inappropriately or sexually abused

What this means
In this part you learn to identify whom to report to if touched inappropriately or sexually abused. You will use ideas from in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify whom to report to if touched inappropriately or sexually abused.
2. Locate, explain, then act responsibly using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Explain: Give one cause and one effect linked to My Family Family members.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify whom to report to if touched inappropriately or sexually abused. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 6: Appreciate the body as a temple of the Holy Spirit and live a holy life

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate the body as a temple of the Holy Spirit and live a holy life. You will use ideas from in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate the body as a temple of the Holy Spirit and live a holy life.
2. Locate, explain, then act responsibly using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Participate: Describe one responsible action a Grade learner can take.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate the body as a temple of the Holy Spirit and live a holy life. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what My Family Family members is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Good citizens follow rules, respect others, and care for shared places.

Kenyan examples: lining up, keeping the compound clean, telling the truth, helping a classmate.

Example 1: Connect “My Family Family members” to a real place or group in Kenya (school, market, county office, home). (skill: name family members in the nuclear and extended family)

Example 2: Give one cause and one effect linked to My Family Family members. (skill: draw a family tree to understand relationships within the family)

Example 3: Describe one responsible action a Grade learner can take. (skill: explain why it is important to honour parents)

Example 4: Connect “My Family Family members” to a real place or group in Kenya (school, market, county office, home). (skill: respect family members for harmonious co- existence)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach My Family Family members to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: name family members in the nuclear and extended family.
3. Practise this skill: draw a family tree to understand relationships within the family.
4. Practise this skill: explain why it is important to honour parents.
5. Make one local Kenya example of My Family Family members from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for My Family Family members: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 4 learner study My Family Family members?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why is it important to know members of your family?
2. Why are healthy family relationships important?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what My Family Family members means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: name family members in the nuclear and extended family.
5. Be able to: draw a family tree to understand relationships within the family.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
